meta.description: Programmatic untargeted LC-MS feature extraction in R with the modern xcms 4.x MsExperiment/XcmsExperiment API, taking raw mzML to a feature table via CentWave peak detection, retention-time alignment, peak-density correspondence, gap-filling, CAMERA redundancy collapse, and built-in QC feature filtering.
meta.re_audit_note: N=9 = the pre-fix audit's 7 regression inputs (1-7) plus 2 new inputs (8-9) never seen by the fixer, per the re-audit protocol. IMPORTANT EXECUTION-COMPLETENESS CAVEAT: only Inputs 3 and 8 were freshly executed to completion within this final scoring session (the 12-file findChromPeaks step for Input 1 did not finish before the audit window closed, and Inputs 2/4/5 depend on Input 1's output). Inputs 1, 2, 4, 5 are scored by direct inspection of the fixed SKILL.md text combined with real, dated numbers from an earlier same-day execution of byte-identical mechanics (peak detection/alignment/correspondence/fill/CAMERA/filter code is unmodified by this fix round; only prose and two default values changed) sitting in this same audit folder. Inputs 6, 7, 9 are reasoning-only by design (Mode A 'correct response' grading), matching the pre-fix audit's own treatment of non-code inputs. See each input's execution_note for the specific basis.

assertions.text: The new small-cohort minFraction guidance produces the behavioral distinction it describes ('minFraction=1.0 requires both replicates present; 0.5 can retain a feature present in only one of the two') on this real n=2 edge case
assertions.note: Real execution: minFraction=1.0 and minFraction=0.5 produced IDENTICAL results (1714 features) on this real 1-case/1-control cohort. minFraction operates per sample-group; with only 1 sample in each group, any value in (0,1] is mathematically equivalent to requiring that single sample. The guidance's worked example ('n=2 per group ... present in both replicates') describes 2 replicates of ONE condition, not a 1-case/1-control pair -- the two scenarios are not the same and the new prose does not disambiguate them, even though this edge-case prompt (like the pre-fix audit's own Input 3) is the 1-case/1-control kind.

recommendations.title: MatchedFilterParam (low-res/quadrupole path) has no worked code example or parameter guidance
recommendations.problem: The Decision Tree and Tips name MatchedFilterParam as the correct tool for low-res/quadrupole/profile-only data, but no code block or fwhm/steps/snthresh guidance exists anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md, unlike CentWaveParam's full worked section and Quantitative Thresholds row.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was authored primarily around the CentWave/high-res path; the low-res alternative was named for completeness but never given the same worked-example treatment.
recommendations.fix: Add a short MatchedFilterParam code block to the Peak Detection section (or a new subsection) with typical binSize/fwhm/steps/snthresh starting points by instrument class, mirroring the CentWave section's structure.

recommendations.title: AutoTuner/IPO (new-instrument path) is a single unelaborated Decision Tree cell
recommendations.problem: This is the only Decision Tree row with zero elaboration anywhere else in the Skill -- no version note, code block, or parameter pointer, unlike every other named tool.
recommendations.root_cause: The row was added to complete the Decision Tree's coverage but was never expanded into its own worked section like the other rows.
recommendations.fix: Add a short paragraph (or explicitly mark out-of-scope with a pointer to AutoTuner's own documentation) describing the recommended entry call and, critically, the mandatory EIC-FWHM verification step already named in the Decision Tree's rationale column.

recommendations.title: New small-cohort minFraction guidance doesn't disambiguate 'n=2 per group' from 'n=2 total, 1 per group'
recommendations.problem: Real execution on a genuine 1-case/1-control (n=2 total) cohort found minFraction=1.0 and 0.5 produce IDENTICAL results (1714 features), because minFraction operates per sample-group and a single-sample group cannot express the 'present in only one of two' distinction the new prose illustrates -- that distinction only holds for 2 replicates of the SAME condition.
recommendations.root_cause: The new Correspondence-section sentence was written with a same-group-replicate example in mind and doesn't flag that a mixed-group case/control pair behaves differently.
recommendations.fix: Add one clause distinguishing '2 replicates of one condition' (minFraction meaningfully varies 0.5 vs 1.0) from '1 sample per condition, no true replicates' (minFraction in (0,1] is equivalent; there is no within-group fraction to tune).
